editorial_control_prompt: Write Stories in Play for Gazzetta di Kyiv with short, penetrating language. Rules: 6 stories exactly; each story must name actors, explain cause->effect, include a contradiction, and be understandable to non-specialists. Card format: title <=9 words; body exactly 2 sentences, 30-52 words. Avoid jargon overload; translate policy into plain power terms (who decides, who pays, who benefits). Must include at least one market channel.

cards.title: Ceasefire Theater, Oil Reality
cards.body: Washington and Tehran talk peace while missiles keep flying, and crude immediately prices the gap. If Hormuz risk stays live, fuel costs rise, inflation pressure returns, and households pay first while governments promise calm.

cards.title: Rate Cuts Are Still Political Fiction
cards.body: Fed officials keep saying inflation is not defeated, especially with energy shocks back in play. Translation: borrowing stays expensive, the dollar stays firm, and voters hear relief while businesses keep paying high financing costs.

cards.title: AI Rally, One Door Exit
cards.body: The AI boom keeps funneling money into the same mega-cap and semiconductor names. Everyone says diversify, yet portfolios crowd into one trade, so one weak earnings print can turn celebration into a synchronized selloff.

cards.title: China EV Surge Hits Tariff Politics
cards.body: China ships cheaper EVs while Washington and Brussels move from complaints to protection. Consumers want price cuts, politicians want domestic jobs, and automakers want time, so autos and battery supply chains now trade on policy headlines as much as demand.

cards.title: LNG Deals Expose Energy Truth
cards.body: Governments keep signing long LNG contracts even while promising fast decarbonization. Public messaging says transition, capital spending says survival, and gas infrastructure keeps winning because energy security beats speeches when factories are on the line.

cards.title: Prediction Markets Meet the Prosecutor
cards.body: Insider-data allegations are dragging prediction markets from trend product to legal target. The crowd works until privileged information enters the room, then trust falls, liquidity thins, and platform valuations reprice in real time.

cards.title: Middle East Risk Premium Re-enters Crude
cards.body: US-Iran strikes have reintroduced a live geopolitical premium into oil and maritime insurance. If corridor risk persists in Hormuz, inflation expectations stay firmer, transport margins compress, and near-term easing odds remain vulnerable.

cards.title: Policy Path Still Inflation-Constrained
cards.body: Fed communication remains inflation-first, keeping the cut path conditional rather than scheduled. Practical effect: support for real yields and USD, with downside pressure concentrated in duration-sensitive equities and rate-dependent financing channels.

cards.title: AI Leadership Remains Concentrated
cards.body: AI capex visibility continues directing equity flows into a narrow semiconductor-hyperscaler cluster. Concentrated positioning is now the core fragility variable, because modest guidance misses can propagate quickly into breadth deterioration and volatility repricing.

cards.title: China EV Momentum Faces Policy Friction
cards.body: China EV export acceleration is colliding with US and EU market-access defenses. Sector pricing now depends as much on tariff sequence and industrial policy timing as on underlying demand, especially across autos, batteries, and metals.

cards.title: LNG Contracts Signal Bloc Formation
cards.body: Long-horizon LNG contracts continue functioning as geopolitical insurance and industrial cost hedges. Capital allocation indicates that energy-security priorities remain structurally dominant, even while official narratives continue emphasizing accelerated decarbonization pathways.

cards.title: Event Markets Reprice Compliance Risk
cards.body: Insider-information allegations raise the probability of tighter enforcement and higher compliance burdens for event-market platforms. Valuation should increasingly depend on market-integrity controls, while weaker operators face faster trust and liquidity deterioration.
